newsitem.title: USA: NY Gov. Pataki proposes compromise on rent rules.
newsitem.headline: NY Gov. Pataki proposes compromise on rent rules.

text.p: New York Gov. George Pataki, who has seen budget talks grind to a halt because of a heated fight over apartment rent rules, has proposed a compromise measure that hinted at including vacancy decontrol.

One of the most controversial aspects of the Republican governor's proposal was expected to be an effort to return the state's 1.1 million regulated apartments, most of which are in New York City, to a free-market system by deregulating empty apartments.

In a one-page statement released Sunday, Pataki said his plan would protect tenants from efforts to force them to quit their apartments. The Democrat-led Assembly, which wants to make permanent the present system, says that in a mid-1970 vacancy decontrol program, landlords harrassed tenants into leaving their apartments, causing the experiment to fail.

Pataki warned that landlords who made life impossible for tenants would pay a stiff price, saying no tenant who needed rent control protection should be subjected to harrassment. "My message to greedy landlords who ignore the law is clear: Harass your tenants and you will pay a price that far exceeds the few extra dollars you may collect from a rent increase."

The governor added that only the top one percent of all tenants in rent regulated apartments -- those who earn more than $175,000 a year -- who he said can afford to pay free market rents, would be asked to do so. The present system sets a $250,000 limit before so-called luxury decontrol rules kick in.

More details about the governor's new plan, which attempts to find the middle ground between the Assembly and the Senate, whose majority leader wants to phase out rent regulations over two to perhaps four years while preserving controls for the needy, disabled and eldery, were expected to be unveiled at a late morning news conference Pataki plans to hold.
